title: Practitioner Exam
description: 40 questions covering all five modules, drawn from a pool of 50. Pass mark is 80%. This is an open-book exam — take your time, browse any module to refresh your memory, or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.prompt: Where in Spoon do you change Look & Feel options?
questions.explanation: Look & Feel and General options are accessed via Tools > Options in the Spoon menu bar.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Configuring PDI

questions.prompt: Which file stores environment-wide variables that PDI loads at startup?
questions.explanation: kettle.properties (typically in ~/.kettle/) holds variables that resolve via ${variable_name} in any transformation or job.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Kettle Variables

questions.scenario: A developer wants a CSV path to come from a Kettle variable named INPUT_PATH instead of being hard-coded in the Text File Input step.
questions.prompt: How do you reference that variable in a transformation field?
questions.explanation: PDI uses ${VAR_NAME} for variable substitution in any field that supports variables (the diamond icon at the right of the field indicates support).
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Kettle Variables

questions.prompt: What is the typical location of kettle.properties on a Windows install?
questions.explanation: PDI looks in %USERPROFILE%\.kettle\ on Windows (and ~/.kettle/ on Linux/macOS) for kettle.properties — a per-user hidden directory.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Kettle Variables

questions.prompt: Which perspective in Spoon shows the canvas where you build transformations?
questions.explanation: The Data Integration perspective is the default canvas for designing transformations and jobs. Other perspectives focus on different tasks.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Configuring PDI

questions.prompt: What is a 'hop' in a PDI transformation?
options: A connection between two steps that passes rows
A retry attempt after a step failure
A row of data flowing through the pipeline
questions.explanation: A hop is the directional connection between two steps — the arrow that passes rows from one step to the next.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Hello World

questions.prompt: What is the difference between 'Run' and 'Preview'?
options: Run executes; Preview shows expected output without executing
Run executes the full transformation; Preview executes only up to a chosen step
questions.explanation: Preview runs the transformation up to the selected step and stops, showing the rows that arrive at that step — useful for incremental debugging.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Hello World

questions.scenario: A developer is debugging a transformation and wants the log to show the actual values inside each row as it passes through a step.
questions.prompt: Which log level produces the most detail, including individual row values?
questions.explanation: Log levels in increasing verbosity: Nothing, Error, Minimal, Basic, Detailed, Debug, RowLevel. RowLevel shows the actual row data and is the most verbose.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Logging

questions.scenario: A transformation occasionally hits rows that fail a database insert, and the developer wants those bad rows routed aside instead of crashing the run.
questions.prompt: How should you handle errors from a step gracefully?
options: Add a try/catch in the JavaScript step
Define error handling on the step and route the error stream to a separate flow
Wrap the transformation in a job with error handling
questions.explanation: PDI's error handling is per-step — right-click a step, configure error handling, then connect the red error hop to a separate stream that processes or logs the bad rows.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Error Handling

questions.scenario: A developer wires a single step's output to two downstream steps and wants to know how PDI splits the rows.
questions.prompt: By default, when a step has two output hops, what happens to the rows?
options: Only the first hop receives data
Rows are split round-robin between the hops
Both hops receive a copy of every row
An error is raised — only one output hop is allowed
questions.explanation: PDI copies rows to all output hops by default ('Copy data to next steps'). You can also configure 'Distribute' on the step to round-robin between hops.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology

questions.prompt: Which step writes a custom message to the execution log per row?
questions.explanation: Write to Log emits a per-row message at a configurable level — handy for inserting checkpoints in your transformation that show in the execution log.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Logging

questions.prompt: When a step has error handling enabled, the error stream emits:
options: The original row plus error_description, error_codes, and error_fields
Just the error message as a single field
questions.explanation: PDI's error handling adds three configurable fields to the rejected row: descriptions, codes, and the field names that triggered the error — letting you process them downstream.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Error Handling

questions.prompt: What does the Abort step do?
options: Skips the current row and continues
Stops the entire transformation immediately with an error
Logs an error and marks the row as a warning
Aborts only the current step; others continue
questions.explanation: Abort stops the whole transformation. Use sparingly — typically when a downstream condition is so wrong (e.g. expected 1000 rows, got 0) that continuing would corrupt data.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Error Handling

questions.prompt: To preview the rows arriving at a specific step without running the full transformation, you would:
options: Right-click the step and choose Preview
Run the transformation, then read the log
Open the step in a separate workspace
questions.explanation: Right-click a step and choose Preview rows. PDI runs upstream steps as needed, captures the rows arriving at the chosen step, and shows them in a grid — fast iteration during build.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Hello World

questions.scenario: A developer is loading a CSV whose first line contains column names rather than data, using a Text File Input step.
questions.prompt: How do you tell the step to treat that first line as a header rather than a data row?
options: Set 'Header is present in first line of file' on the Content tab
Set 'Skip first row' on the Fields tab
Add a Filter Rows step downstream
Set 'First data line' to 2 on the General tab
questions.explanation: The Content tab has the 'Header' checkbox; when checked, the first row is treated as field names rather than data.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Text File Input

questions.prompt: Which expression language does the JSON Input step use to extract fields from a JSON document?
questions.explanation: JSONPath ($.array[*].field) is the JSON equivalent of XPath. JSON Input uses JSONPath expressions to navigate JSON structures.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Read JSON

questions.prompt: The 'Get data from XML' step uses which expression language to select nodes?
questions.explanation: XPath expressions select nodes from XML documents — Get data from XML uses XPath to map source nodes to PDI fields.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Read XML

questions.scenario: A developer is loading a customer table and must update a customer's row if the key already exists, or insert a new row if it does not.
questions.prompt: Which step performs this insert-or-update based on a key match?
questions.explanation: Insert/Update finds rows by lookup key — updates if found, inserts if not. 'Update' only updates existing rows; 'Table Output' only inserts.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Table Insert/Update

questions.prompt: Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 retains:
options: Only the latest value of each attribute
A single version flag per row, with no history
Full history with effective-date ranges per row
Only changes since the last load
questions.explanation: SCD Type 2 keeps a row per change with valid-from / valid-to dates, allowing point-in-time queries against historical attribute values.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Slowly Changing Dimensions

questions.scenario: A developer needs to read and write objects in a MinIO bucket running on-premises.
questions.prompt: How would you connect to that MinIO bucket from PDI?
questions.explanation: MinIO speaks the S3 protocol, so PDI's S3 VFS connection (or named connection) handles MinIO the same as AWS S3.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — MinIO

questions.prompt: Which step reads rows from a relational database using a SELECT statement?
questions.explanation: Table Input executes a SQL SELECT against the configured connection and emits each result row downstream as a PDI row.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Reading from a Database

questions.prompt: The Excel Writer step can be configured to:
options: Either create or append, depending on the 'Append' option
Append rows but never modify existing rows
questions.explanation: Excel Writer's 'Append' option controls whether rows are appended to an existing sheet/file or a fresh one is created — both modes are supported.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Excel Writer

questions.scenario: A nightly export produces millions of rows and the team wants each output file capped at a manageable size.
questions.prompt: In Text File Output, what does the 'Split every... rows' option do?
options: Filters out rows once a count is exceeded
Creates a new output file every N rows
Limits the input rows read per execution
questions.explanation: Set 'Split every... rows' to N (e.g. 10000) and Text File Output rolls to a new file every N rows. Useful for chunking large outputs.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Text File Output

questions.scenario: A developer sets up a new connection to a MySQL database but Spoon reports that the driver cannot be found.
questions.prompt: What must be available for PDI to connect to MySQL?
options: The MySQL CLI tool on PATH
The MySQL JDBC driver JAR in data-integration/lib/
questions.explanation: PDI uses JDBC for all database connections. Drop the MySQL JDBC driver JAR (mysql-connector-j-*.jar) into the data-integration/lib/ folder so the classpath picks it up.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Connecting to a Database

questions.prompt: For a Merge Join to work correctly, both inputs must:
options: Have the same number of rows
Be sorted on the join key in the same direction
questions.explanation: Merge Join walks both streams in lockstep, so they must arrive sorted on the join key. Add Sort Rows steps upstream or use ORDER BY in the source query.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Merge Join

questions.prompt: The Combination Lookup / Update step is typically used for:
options: Junk dimensions — assigning surrogate keys to combinations of low-cardinality fields
questions.explanation: Combination Lookup/Update inserts a row for each new combination of input fields and reuses the existing surrogate key on subsequent occurrences — perfect for 'junk' dimensions.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Slowly Changing Dimensions

questions.scenario: A developer is reading a CSV where some text fields are wrapped in double quotes because they contain commas.
questions.prompt: What is the correct way to parse those quoted fields in Text File Input?
options: Set Enclosure to the quote character on the Content tab
Use the Calculator step to parse them after the read
Strip the quotes manually with Modified JavaScript Value
CSVs with embedded commas cannot be read by Text File Input
questions.explanation: The Enclosure field (typically a double quote) tells Text File Input which character wraps fields containing commas — standard for proper CSV parsing.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Text File Input

questions.prompt: Which statements correctly contrast Database Join with Merge Join? (Select all that apply.)
options: Database Join executes a SQL query per incoming row
Merge Join requires both inputs sorted on the join key
Database Join is always faster than Merge Join on large datasets
Merge Join executes a SQL query per incoming row
questions.explanation: Database Join runs SQL per incoming row (flexible but slower for big lookups). Merge Join requires both inputs sorted on the join key, then walks both streams in lockstep — it issues no per-row SQL.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Database Join

questions.prompt: Which step produces the Cartesian product of two streams?
questions.explanation: Join Rows (Cartesian product) outputs every combination of rows from both inputs — N x M output rows from N and M inputs.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Join Rows

questions.scenario: A transformation runs millions of input rows through a Database Lookup against a small, static reference table, and the developer wants to cut the repeated database round-trips.
questions.prompt: What does enabling caching on the Database Lookup avoid?
options: Repeated SQL queries for the same lookup key
questions.explanation: With cache enabled, lookup results are held in memory; subsequent lookups for the same key skip the database round-trip — a major speed-up for high-volume input streams.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Database Lookups

questions.prompt: Merge Rows (diff) compares two sorted streams and sets a flag on each row. Which flag values can it produce? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Merge Rows (diff) emits each row with a flagfield of new, changed, deleted, or identical between the reference and compare streams — the building block for change-data-capture patterns.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Merge Rows (diff)

questions.prompt: Which scripting step is best suited for spreadsheet-style expressions like IF, SUM, or CONCAT?
questions.explanation: Formula uses LibreOffice-style expressions. Modified JavaScript Value is for procedural per-row JavaScript; Calculator is for a fixed set of math operations only (no free-form expressions).
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Formula

questions.scenario: A developer needs to enrich a large order stream with values from a small, fixed reference set of country codes.
questions.prompt: When should you prefer Stream Lookup over Database Lookup?
options: When the lookup table is small and fits in memory
When the lookup table is huge
questions.explanation: Stream Lookup loads the entire reference set into memory before the main stream. Fast for small dimensions; bad if the reference doesn't fit in available RAM.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Lookups

questions.prompt: The Group By step requires its input to be:
questions.explanation: Group By accumulates within each group as it sees consecutive same-key rows. Without sorting, it splits a single group across multiple output rows. Use Sort Rows upstream.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset

questions.prompt: Modified JavaScript Value differs from Calculator in that:
options: Modified JavaScript Value can implement arbitrary per-row logic with conditionals; Calculator is limited to a fixed set of operations
Calculator runs row-by-row; Modified JavaScript Value runs in batches
questions.explanation: Calculator offers a dropdown of built-in operations (add, multiply, date diff, etc.) — fast and clear. Modified JavaScript Value is full JavaScript per row — flexible but slower and harder to debug.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Modified JavaScript Value

questions.scenario: A developer needs to remove duplicate rows from a stream based on a single key field.
questions.prompt: Which approach deduplicates the stream correctly?
questions.explanation: Unique Rows requires sorted input — it compares the current row only against the previous one. Sort first by the dedup key, then Unique Rows drops the duplicates.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset

questions.scenario: A developer adds a Filter Rows step with the condition qty > 0 and wonders how the matching and non-matching rows are routed.
questions.prompt: What does Filter Rows produce?
options: Two output streams — true (matching) and false (non-matching)
It skips the step entirely if no false hop is connected
questions.explanation: Filter Rows has both a 'send true rows to step' and a 'send false rows to step' hop. You can wire either or both — unwired hops simply discard those rows.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset

questions.prompt: A PDI job differs from a transformation in that:
options: Jobs orchestrate transformations and other entries (run-this-then-that)
questions.explanation: Transformations move rows step-by-step; jobs orchestrate at a higher level — running transformations, sending mail, copying files, and branching on success/failure.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Hello World Job

questions.scenario: In a job, a developer wants a follow-on entry to run only when the preceding entry completes successfully.
questions.prompt: What does a job hop labelled 'evaluation: success' mean?
options: The next entry runs only if the previous one succeeded
The next entry runs only if the previous one failed
The next entry runs in parallel with the previous one
questions.explanation: Job hops can be unconditional, follow-on-success, or follow-on-failure. A 'success' hop fires only when the source entry returned success.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Order of Execution

questions.prompt: A parameter passed to a transformation is:
options: Set at runtime and accessible via ${param_name}
questions.explanation: Parameters are set when invoking the transformation (CLI, parent job, scheduler) and resolve via ${name}. They override kettle.properties values for that specific run.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Parameters

questions.prompt: Which of the following are valid PDI run configuration targets? (Select all that apply.)
options: Carte / clustered (Pentaho engine on remote nodes)
questions.explanation: Run configurations target the Pentaho (Kettle) engine — locally in Spoon (the default, non-editable 'Pentaho local') or remotely via Carte master/slave nodes and cluster schemas. 'Embedded JVM container' and a 'binary execution plan file' are not run-configuration options.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.prompt: Pan and Kitchen are:
options: Command-line runners — Pan for transformations, Kitchen for jobs
questions.explanation: pan.sh / pan.bat runs a .ktr (transformation); kitchen.sh / kitchen.bat runs a .kjb (job). Used for scheduled production runs and CI.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.prompt: The default value for a transformation parameter is set:
options: In kettle.properties on the runtime host
In the transformation's Parameters tab (Edit > Settings)
In the parent job's Parameters tab when calling the transformation
All of the above — values resolve in that order at runtime
questions.explanation: The transformation's Parameters tab declares the parameter and its default. A parent job can override it and kettle.properties can supply a base; at runtime an explicit caller value wins, otherwise the transformation's default is used.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Parameters

questions.scenario: A developer wants the operations team emailed automatically once a nightly load job finishes.
questions.prompt: Which job entry sends that email?
questions.explanation: The Mail job entry sends configurable SMTP email — typically wired to the success or failure hop of a key transformation so you (or ops) get pinged on the outcome.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Jobs

questions.prompt: A variable defined in kettle.properties is:
options: Available globally across all transformations and jobs at runtime
Available only inside transformations, not jobs
Available only after a Set Variables step
Available only on the master in a clustered run
questions.explanation: kettle.properties is loaded on PDI startup; its values are accessible via ${var_name} from any transformation or job for the lifetime of the process.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Parameters and Variables

questions.prompt: The Pentaho Repository can be:
questions.explanation: PDI supports file-based repositories (a folder of .ktr/.kjb on disk, version-controlled by the user) or database repositories backed by Pentaho Server's metadata store.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution

questions.prompt: Carte and Kitchen differ in that:
options: Carte runs interactively; Kitchen runs as a service
Kitchen is a CLI runner (one-shot); Carte is a long-running HTTP server
They are identical with different names
Kitchen is for transformations and Carte is for jobs
questions.explanation: Kitchen runs a job to completion and exits — perfect for cron. Carte stays up listening on HTTP for execution requests — used for slave servers and clustered runs.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.scenario: A clustered transformation runs across one Carte master and two slave nodes.
questions.prompt: What is the master's role in that clustered run?
options: Distributes work to the slaves and aggregates their results
Holds the database connection pool only
questions.explanation: The master orchestrates: it distributes input rows to the slaves, collects their results, and emits the aggregated stream. The slaves do the heavy work in parallel.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations
